page.text:
When $A$ is contained in $B$ but the two sets are not identical, we say
that $A$ is a *proper subset* of $B$, denoted $A \subsetneq B$. This
requires two independent conditions: every element of $A$ must belong to
$B$, and $B$ must contain at least one element $b$ such that $b \notin
A$. Proper inclusion constitutes a strict partial order on collections
of sets.
